what_it_does: checks duplicate ids, parent links, parent cycles, required roles and team membership of every workstream, returning error strings

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the four team collections depend only on people_data and are rebuilt, with lowercasing set comprehensions, once per workstream; building them once before the loop removes (workstreams-1) rebuilds of three sets

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `kind` and `parent_kind` are bound per workstream and never read; deleting the two statements removes a dict lookup, a .get and a subscript per workstream. Separate edit from a

what_it_does: inserts a member entry into the Emeritus section of a README, keeping member lines sorted by display name

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the same `re.match(r'^[-*+] \[', line)` runs for every line twice (once for member_lines, once for first/last index); computing the member flag once per line halves the regex calls

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: member-line and sort-key patterns are passed as strings to re.match on each use; module-level compiled patterns skip the re cache probe per call. Separate edit from a

what_it_does: returns, for each user in `remaining`, the first matching cached event of the repo

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: once every user in `remaining` has an entry in `found`, the rest of the cached events cannot change the result; breaking there stops scanning of up to thousands of events

what_it_does: walks repos and checks maintainer activity via comments, reviews, authored-PR GraphQL search and merge events, shrinking `remaining`

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `_search_fields()` depends only on global DEBUG and is called per user; hoisting one call above the user loop removes a call per user

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: the sanitising re.sub is evaluated twice per user in a batch; compute once into a list of (user, safe)

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: `remaining` is non-empty at 658: the function returned at 618 if empty and the batch loop returns when it empties, so the test is always true

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: `Looks like it, but is not`: the two passes print different debug text (`PR comments` vs `issue comments`) and use different comment_type, so merging them changes DEBUG output

what_it_does: walks repos and checks approver activity via PR comments, issue comments and reviews

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: merging the two _check_comments passes would change the DEBUG output text per user (`PR comments` vs `issue comments`), which is part of the unit's printed output

what_it_does: batched GraphQL search for reviewed-by PRs for up to 10 users, REST-verifying candidates and paginating

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the sanitising re.sub for the alias is run twice per user (in the alias builder and in the result reader); build once per batch

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `if not batch_users` cannot be true: slices start below len(remaining_list); the branch is evaluated for nothing per batch

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: verification stops at the first confirmed PR; running them concurrently would issue extra requests and parallelism does not save energy here

what_it_does: pages through repo issue comments since cutoff and builds {user: {pr: [...], issue: [...]}} cached per repo

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `number not in commenters[user][kind]` is a linear scan of a growing list per comment; a local set of (user, kind, number) answers membership in O(1) while the returned lists keep their order

what_it_does: for each repo, rewrites the README removing inactive members and adding them to Emeritus, then forks and opens a PR

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: readme is rewritten after every user, so the section offsets and text change between iterations; no small edit hoists the lookup without changing results

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: the member list is parsed from text that is mutated per user; an index would be stale after _remove_member_line, and there are only a handful of members

what_it_does: removes one user's line from a named README section and returns the modified readme or None

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: search readme with pattern.search(readme, start, end) and cut readme[:ms]+readme[me:], so the section copy and the three-piece rebuild with a second copy go away; start is a line start so ^ behaves identically

what_it_does: orchestrates team discovery, activity checks and the printed inactive report

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `r in args.repo` list scan per repo per team; a set of args.repo is O(1). Cannot be measured here: main needs a token, the network and argv

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: user_repo_role.setdefault(user, {}) runs once per repo of every team entry; hoisting one per user avoids the repeated dict creation and lookup. Cannot be measured here for the same reasons as a

what_it_does: follows Link headers to collect all pages of a REST listing

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: break once rel=next is found; GitHub sends one next link so the rest of the split parts are scanned for nothing. Network-bound, cannot be measured here

what_it_does: renders one markdown table of SIGs from workstream dicts

decisions.label: b

what_it_does: renders the per-SIG detail sections of one group

decisions.why: detail text grown with += per SIG; collect in a list and join

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: each stale handle compiles a new regex (distinct pattern, so a real compile each time) and rescans the body; one combined regex of all stale handles removes them in one pass. Separate edit from a

what_it_does: looks up the GitHub login of every devstats name over HTTP and builds [login, contributions] rows

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: independent per-name lookups run serially, each with a 100 ms sleep; a small thread pool would overlap the waits (energy effect uncertain; needs the network, cannot be measured)

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: the REST users endpoint has no batch form; a GraphQL redesign would change the unit's contract and rate-limit behaviour

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: `for i in range(len(names))` indexing two parallel lists; zip(names, contributions) is the idiom. Network-bound, cannot be measured

what_it_does: fetches one user's canonical GitHub login

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: requests.get opens a fresh TLS connection per lookup; a module-level requests.Session reuses connections across the loop in build_devstats_rows. Network-bound, cannot be measured

what_it_does: fetches workflow runs and jobs via gh and returns per-job duration records for bare-metal runners

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: parse_iso(started) is evaluated up to three times per job; parse once. Needs gh and the network, cannot be measured

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: GitHub offers no endpoint that lists jobs for many runs, so one request per run is needed

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: list() is deliberate: errors from the gh subprocess are raised during iteration and the try/except around it must see them before any record is added

what_it_does: aggregates job records per (repo, workflow) and renders a Markdown table

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `runs` set duplicates the key set of `run_totals`, updated on the next line; dropping it and using len(run_totals) saves a set add per record
